story.title: OTP multi-factor login for web and mobile banking
story.description: Add a one-time passcode (OTP) step to customer login on web-banking and mobile-banking. The authentication-service generates, sends and verifies six-digit codes with a five-minute expiry; the notification-service delivers each code by SMS to the customer's verified mobile number; customer-db stores the MFA enrolment flag and verified phone number in two new columns. The API gateway exposes new /auth/otp/send and /auth/otp/verify endpoints. Lock the login after five failed codes and record every attempt for audit.
acceptance_criteria: Customers enrolled in MFA must enter a valid six-digit OTP after their password before a session is issued.
Codes expire after five minutes and five failed attempts lock the login for 30 minutes.
OTP SMS messages are delivered within 30 seconds through the notification service.
Every OTP send, success and failure is recorded for audit.

requirement.business_summary: Web and mobile banking customers will be required to complete a one-time passcode (OTP) step after entering their password when they are enrolled in multi-factor authentication. The six-digit code is sent by SMS to the customer's verified mobile number, expires after five minutes, and five failed codes lock the login for 30 minutes. Every OTP send, success and failure is recorded for audit.
requirement.technical_summary: The authentication-service is extended to generate, deliver and verify six-digit OTPs with a five-minute expiry, enforce a five-failed-attempt lockout for 30 minutes, and emit audit records for every send, success and failure. Codes are dispatched as SMS via the notification-service to the customer's verified mobile number. The customer-db adds two columns to hold the MFA enrolment flag and the verified phone number. The api-gateway exposes two new routes, /auth/otp/send and /auth/otp/verify. The web-banking and mobile-banking login flows gain an OTP entry step between password entry and session issuance for MFA-enrolled customers.
requirement.business_domain: Retail Digital Banking — Customer Authentication and Access
affected_capabilities: One-time passcode generation, expiry and verification
Login lockout after repeated failed OTP attempts
Customer MFA enrolment and verified phone number storage
requirement.engineering_scope: Contained change spanning six components: new OTP generation/verification and lockout logic in authentication-service; a new OTP SMS notification in notification-service; two new columns (MFA enrolment flag, verified phone number) in customer-db; two new gateway routes (/auth/otp/send, /auth/otp/verify) in api-gateway; and an OTP entry step in the web-banking and mobile-banking login screens. No changes to balances, payments, cards or loan processing; audit attempt records are written as new entries to the existing append-only audit store without schema change. Thresholds (five-minute expiry, five attempts, 30-minute lockout) are configuration/business rules local to the authentication flow.

story.title: Self-service password reset
story.description: Let customers reset a forgotten password themselves from web-banking and mobile-banking. The authentication-service issues a single-use reset token that expires in 15 minutes and enforces the password policy; the notification-service sends the reset link by email and SMS; customer-db records the last reset time and failed reset attempts. Reset requests must not reveal whether an account exists.
acceptance_criteria: A customer can request a reset link and set a new password that meets the password policy.
Reset tokens are single use and expire after 15 minutes.
The response is identical whether or not the account exists.
Five reset requests in an hour block further requests for that customer.

requirement.business_summary: Customers will be able to reset a forgotten password themselves from web-banking and mobile-banking instead of relying on assisted servicing. Authentication Service issues a single-use reset token valid for 15 minutes and enforces the password policy; Notification Service delivers the reset link by email and SMS; Customer Database records the last reset time and failed reset attempts. Reset requests return an identical response whether or not the account exists, and five requests in an hour block further requests for that customer.
requirement.technical_summary: Add a self-service password reset flow: Authentication Service gains reset-token issuance/validation (single use, 15-minute expiry), password-policy enforcement, uniform request responses to prevent account enumeration, and per-customer rate limiting of five reset requests per hour. Web and mobile channels add request-reset and set-new-password UI and call the new endpoints. Notification Service sends the reset link over email and SMS. Customer Database stores the last reset time and failed reset attempt count for the customer. No card or financial/ledger data is involved.
requirement.business_domain: Identity and Access Management / Retail Banking Self-Service
affected_capabilities: Reset token issuance and expiry control
Reset request rate limiting / abuse prevention
Email and SMS notification delivery for security events
requirement.engineering_scope: Contained, single-flow change. Authentication Service: new reset-token issue/validate logic (single use, 15-minute expiry), password-policy enforcement on the new password, identical responses regardless of account existence, and a per-customer limit of five reset requests per hour. Web Banking and Mobile Banking: add request-reset and set-new-password screens wired to those endpoints. Notification Service: send the reset link via existing email and SMS channels. Customer Database: persist last reset time and failed reset attempt count for the customer record. No changes to payment, card, loan or ledger processing; no changes to existing public contracts beyond adding the new self-service endpoints.

story.title: Increase daily payment limits for premium customers
story.description: Increase daily payment limits for premium customers from AED 25,000 to AED 50,000 for domestic transfers. The payment-service must obtain premium eligibility and the effective account limit from account-service before accepting each payment. Keep fraud screening active through fraud-engine and use the transaction ledger in transaction-db to calculate the remaining daily allowance, including concurrent requests. Roll out the business rule behind an approved feature flag during the payments release window. Operations must confirm threshold monitoring and rollback readiness before enabling the higher limit; standard customer limits remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A premium account can submit domestic payments totaling AED 50,000 per bank-local calendar day; the next payment is declined.
A standard account retains its AED 25,000 daily limit and existing per-payment checks.
Concurrent payment submissions cannot exceed the account daily limit, and retries create one transaction ledger posting.
Every accepted payment passes fraud screening; operations approves monitoring and can restore the previous limit with the feature flag.

requirement.engineering_scope: A small, contained change: payment-service modified to fetch premium eligibility and limit from account-service, compute remaining allowance using transaction-db reads, enforce the new limit via a feature flag; account-service updated to expose premium eligibility/effective limit; feature flag configuration added.
